subject: Dedicated cluster options and ramp scenarios — Vermillion Bio
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@vermillionbio.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity planning — high-level ask

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the call earlier. Vermillion is trying to lock a Dedicated capacity path we can attach to the contract. A few constraints from our side:

- Production peak: ~1.2k concurrent token-generator requests across 20–30s tail latency target.
- Burst windows for nightly batch runs (2–3 hours) where throughput needs jump ~3x.
- Security: VPC private deployment required; per-route logging and 90-day retention.
- Timeline: we'd like a staged activation that lands before end of Q1.

Can you send a short set of options (cluster size, minimum committed GPUs, ramp schedule and fallback) that align to a mid-market seat/throughput profile? Procurement will need the options for our internal evaluation.

Thanks —
Lydia
VP Infrastructure
Vermillion Bio

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@vermillionbio.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Dec 2025 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — high-level ask

Lydia —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached is a short playbook and three practical reservation options designed to meet the production + burst profile you described. Summary below, full details in the attached PDF and costing sheet.

Option A — Conservative (lower committed spend)
- Cluster: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (shared lanes)
- Min committed GPUs: 8
- Ramp: 2-week activation (warm-start single pod -> scale to 8)
- Burst: Gateway burst to hosted pool for 2x sustained bursts (credits apply)
- Good when: predictability isn’t critical, cost sensitivity is high

Option B — Balanced (recommended for your profile)
- Cluster: 24 x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool)
- Min committed GPUs: 16 (baseline guaranteed)
- Ramp: 4-week staged rollout (8 -> 16 -> 24) with warm-cache prefill windows
- Burst: Elastic burst slot to extend to 48 for scheduled nightly batch windows (rate-limited)
- Notes: includes 48 hours of warm-start credits and on-call SRE during first 2 weeks

Option C — Performance-first (shortest latency/highest throughput)
- Cluster: 64 x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Min committed GPUs: 48
- Ramp: 1-week accelerated activation with pre-warmed KV caches
- Burst: Native within-cluster bursting to 2x capacity; minimal hosted fallback
- Good when: SLA commitments require tight p99 latency and no external fallbacks

Thoughts on trade-offs: Option B balances cost and reliability for the workload you described — it provides headroom for the 3x nightly bursts while keeping a reasonable committed floor. If procurement prefers smaller upfront commitments we can shift to Option A with an explicit multi-stage trigger to move to B once usage thresholds hit.

Attachments: vermillion_capacity_playbook_v2.pdf, vermillion_proposal_costing_sheet.xlsx

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call to walk through the math.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Thu, Dec 11, 2025 at 11:03 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Lydia —
> 
> Appreciate the clarity. Attached is a short playbook and three practical reservation options...

Quick tech note from my side: for the 24->48 burst pattern in Option B we recommend enabling KV prefix caching for the top 20% of prompt families and a persistent prefill job during the 2 hours before the batch window. That reduces cold-start tail by ~25%.

Also recommend adding a "warm-start credit" bucket in the contract for the first 30 days so we can pre-warm additional model variants if you decide to expand across embeddings/chat endpoints. If procurement prefers the staged trigger, we should include explicit usage thresholds (tokens/s or p50 RPS) to auto-advance the ramp.

I'll sync with Ben on pricing levers (quantization + burst credits) and have a draft cost appendix by tomorrow EOD.

—Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime

From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@vermillionbio.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@vermillionbio.com
Date: Fri, 12 Dec 2025 14:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — high-level ask

Tessa / Karthik —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear options. Procurement prefers Option B (the balanced path), provided we can:

- Get a documented SLA on p95/p99 latency for the baseline (16 GPU) lane or explicit fallback behavior if the baseline is saturated.
- See an estimated monthly cost with the staged ramp and an explicit line for scheduled burst credits.
- Confirm the VPC onboarding checklist and the timeline for access to logging/audit exports.

Please send the revised proposal (cost breakdown + SLA language + onboarding checklist) and the DocuSign-ready contract. Procurement is targeting an internal review next week.

Best,
Lydia
VP Infrastructure
Vermillion Bio
